verification_notes: Audited from first principles: Misconception that normal incidence light experiences no refraction verified. Refraction is fundamentally defined by change in phase velocity v = c/n and wavelength lambda = lambda_0 / n. At normal incidence (i = 0), Snell's Law yields r = 0, giving zero angular deviation delta = |i - r| = 0. However, phase speed decreases by factor n_1 / n_2 and wavelength compresses by factor n_1 / n_2. Partial transmission and reflection occur according to Fresnel's normal incidence equations R = ((n_1 - n_2)/(n_1 + n_2))^2. Physical refutation, distinction between wave refraction and geometric ray deviation, and corrective pedagogical exposition verified.
